queries: The adaptive traffic signal system operates through a decentralized gradient descent mechanism where each intersection continuously adjusts its timing parameters based on local performance metrics and neighbor information. Each intersection measures its own performance (vehicle throughput, queue length) and receives performance metrics from adjacent intersections. It then calculates a gradient indicating how to adjust green-split to improve its performance while considering neighbor performance. The adjustment is proportional to the local gradient and inversely proportional to the sum of neighbor performance metrics, creating a distributed optimization process.
sources: The Lotus Effect: Superhydrophobicity and Self-Cleaning
